correctness.rationale: The proof identifies precisely all cyclic six-polytope facets using Gale evenness, proves H_8 path parity components via exhaustive enumeration and propagates them to every larger path by a covering matching lemma. For even n each cycle facet stays balanced, while for odd n one exhibited wrap-edge facet joins the two path components; C_7 is checked directly. Unique facet unions give all edges, and E-V+1 determines the integral wedge ranks. Standalone verify.py was executed and returned ALL_VERIFY_OK, including independent Gale checks and finite range tests.

originality.rationale: The primary 2025 r-tupling paper defines the construction and proves weak Cohen-Macaulay connectivity bounds, not the precise graph component structure or circle counts. Available older calculations concern different block sizes and dimensions. Explicit published-finding corpus and literature searches of three-tupling, Gale matching facets, parity classes, and exact circle ranks did not identify a dominating result. This is a best-knowledge assessment, not a proof of global uniqueness.
residual_risks: The October 2026 revision of arXiv:2506.10436 was not fully inspected; the accessible first-version full text was read.
Exact newest-version coverage is therefore a residual originality uncertainty, not a claim of complete literature exclusion.

value.rationale: For the natural three-tupling of the first six-dimensional cyclic neighborly-sphere family, the theorem supplies a complete all-parameter homotopy classification. It exposes a sharp parity-driven change in connectedness and computes two distinct growing integral fundamental-group ranks in even order. This cannot be inferred from the known r-tupling wCM estimates or the previously separate r=2 and r=4 cases, and supplies a reusable path-to-cycle matching connectivity method.
